leagues.quote: Se jugarán dos torneos cortos en el año, el Apertura y Clausura, ambos bajo el mismo formato. ... Finalmente para determinar el campeón de la temporada, se jugará una serie final a partido único entre los campeones de cada uno de los torneos cortos.
leagues.note: 14 clubs. Each short tournament is its own three-stage competition: 13-round round-robin, top 8 into two semifinal groups of 4 (6 rounds), then a single-match final; that winner takes a Libertadores place. The absolute champion is decided by a single-match Final Absoluta between the Apertura and Clausura winners (automatic title if one club wins both), played in December - the season closes on 13 December per the infobox. Points from both short tournaments sum into the tabla acumulada, which allocates the remaining continental berths and relegates its last-placed team (1 down). Windows from the sub-articles: Apertura 29 January - 7 June, Clausura 31 July - 29 November.

leagues.quote: El torneo de Segunda División tuvo la misma modalidad para dos torneos cortos, un Apertura y un Clausura, de la siguiente manera: Fase regular: 16 equipos se dividieron en dos grupos por su ubicación geográfica.
leagues.note: The Apertura/Clausura label is not what was played. The article's own fixture is one continuous season of 34 matchdays (Fecha 1-34, from 21 February 2026, breaking for the World Cup in June-July) and it carries a single pair of group tables (Grupo Occidental 9 clubs + Grupo Oriental 8 = 17 clubs) in which teams already have 31 matches played - impossible for two 14-round short tournaments. So as played this is one long double round-robin split into two geographic groups, not two phases; the Formato section still describes the announced Apertura/Clausura plus two-legged Final Absoluta for promotion, and no eliminatoria or Final Absoluta data exists yet. Last matchday and the promotion/relegation rules are not documented, hence champion/relegation unknown.
